bug_description.original: A global-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) occurs in xmlStrndup (xmlstring.c) when invoked from the HTML parser (HTMLparser.c) during DOCTYPE/system/public literal parsing (e.g., htmlParseSystemLiteral/htmlParseDocTypeDecl). The parser can supply an incorrect length/offset to xmlStrndup, causing it to read past the end of a buffer into adjacent global memory. This can crash the process and may lead to memory corruption or information disclosure.
bug_description.normalized: In the vulnerable HTML DOCTYPE literal parsers, `htmlParseSystemLiteral` and `htmlParsePubidLiteral` advance `CUR_PTR` with `NEXT` after reaching the closing quote but before calling `xmlStrndup((BASE_PTR + startPosition), len)`. That sequencing reuses the original start offset and the previously accumulated `len` after parser state has moved past the literal terminator. For the saved witness, the resulting source pointer and length handed to `xmlStrndup` make `memcpy` read past the parser buffer into adjacent global storage, producing the observed global-buffer-overflow. The fix moves `NEXT` after `xmlStrndup`, preserving the pre-advance state during duplication.

source.description: First project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled system-literal slice as an offset into the parser input buffer.
source.value_from: The saved testcase bytes contain `<!DOCTYPEs SYSTEM" "`. In the reproduced push-parser path (`htmlParseChunk` -> `htmlParseTryOrFinish` -> `htmlParseDocTypeDecl` -> `htmlParseExternalID`), `htmlParseSystemLiteral` consumes that quoted literal from the attacker-controlled document buffer and snapshots its starting offset with `startPosition = CUR_PTR - BASE_PTR;`.

sink.description: ASan sink. `xmlStrndup` copies the parser-supplied byte range and, for the saved witness, reads past the parser buffer into adjacent global storage.
sink.note: Both saved ASan traces report a `global-buffer-overflow` at `xmlstring.c:53:5`, with the faulting address between adjacent globals in `parserInternals.c`.

root_cause.description: The parser advances past the closing quote before duplicating the literal, then still duplicates from the old start offset with the previously accumulated length.
root_cause.note: Patch `1061537efdf3874c91fd50d18f98c4b8a3518e52` moves `NEXT` after `xmlStrndup` in both `htmlParseSystemLiteral` and `htmlParsePubidLiteral`, confirming that this pre-copy state advance was the missing sequencing obligation.

tainted_value_origin.note: The libFuzzer harness passes the remaining testcase bytes as the HTML document buffer. The saved reproduction report says `./fuzz/html -runs=1 /gt/poc` reproduced the issue and the saved sanitizer trace shows the later crash from `htmlParseChunk` line 74.

parser_admitted.description: In the accepted push-parser continuation, the testcase chunk is recognized as a DOCTYPE declaration and routed into DOCTYPE parsing.

coarse_trace.summary: The push parser recognizes `<!DOCTYPE` in the testcase chunk and dispatches to `htmlParseDocTypeDecl`.
DOCTYPE external-ID parsing matches the `SYSTEM` keyword, skips blanks, and calls `htmlParseSystemLiteral` on the attacker-controlled quoted literal.
The parser snapshots the literal start and counts bytes until the closing quote.
Vulnerable sequencing advances past the closing quote before `xmlStrndup`, while still reusing the old start offset and accumulated length.
`xmlStrndup` allocates `len + 1` bytes and trusts the parser-provided `cur` and `len`.
`memcpy` reads beyond the parser buffer into adjacent global storage, matching the saved ASan report.

fine_trace.note: Source. After `htmlParseExternalID` has matched the testcase's `SYSTEM` external ID and consumed the opening quote, the parser records the attacker-controlled literal start as an offset into the current input buffer.
The scan loop advances across each literal payload byte until `CUR == quote`, incrementing `len` for the bytes seen before the terminating quote while leaving `startPosition` unchanged.
The caller enters the `SYSTEM` branch and requests a system literal. This is the control bridge from the saved stack frame `htmlParseExternalID:3305` into the vulnerable literal parser.

Root cause. Once `CUR` is the closing quote, `NEXT` advances parser state past that terminator before duplication. The later `xmlStrndup((BASE_PTR+startPosition), len)` still uses the previously captured start offset and accumulated length from the pre-advance scan, so the copied byte range no longer matches the parser state at the call site.
`xmlStrndup` trusts the parser-supplied `cur` and `len` from step 4 and allocates a destination buffer sized for exactly that requested copy length plus the terminator.

Sink. `memcpy` reads the full parser-supplied range. For the saved witness, the read crosses out of the parser buffer and into adjacent globals in `parserInternals.c`, matching both saved ASan reports and the reproduced stack `xmlStrndup <- htmlParseExternalID:3305 <- htmlParseDocTypeDecl:3703`.

poc.trigger: The saved testcase is a raw `fuzz/html.c` input whose visible bytes contain `<meta charset=TSCII><!DOCTYPEs SYSTEM" "` followed by non-ASCII bytes. In the reproduced push-parser path, that witness is sufficient to reach DOCTYPE external-ID parsing and then `htmlParseSystemLiteral`, where the vulnerable pre-copy `NEXT` leads to the out-of-bounds read reported by ASan.

format.name: libxml2-html-fuzzer
format.contract: The validated trigger is the saved `fuzz/html.c` witness containing the exact `SYSTEM" "` structure that reaches `htmlParseExternalID`'s `SYSTEM` branch and then `htmlParseSystemLiteral`. Grounded by the staged source and the saved ASan traces, this GT does not generalize beyond that witnessed layout; it claims only that this concrete input reaches the vulnerable pre-copy `NEXT` sequence and then the observed global-buffer-overflow in `xmlStrndup`.
